newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares dampened by economy concerns.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares dampened by economy concerns.

text.p: A lack of positive indicators for the Singapore economy was likely to keep share prices flat for the foreseeable future, dealers said on Thursday.
"The economy is not ticking up yet as we thought it would and so I think the market will be kind of sideways for some time," said one dealer with a local firm.
A flat opening of the Straits Times Industrials Index, which stood barely changed at 1,966.82, up 0.41 at 0230 GMT, was indicative of lagging sentiment.
Small cap and electronics stocks were early risers while blue chips languished mainly in negative territory.
IPC Corp shares led the early actives with 10.5 million shares traded out of a market total of 51 million by 0230 GMT.
The stock rose Singapore $0.015 to S$0.555 after posting better than expected interim results on Wednesday evening.
Fellow technology firm Venture Manufacturing recouped some of the ground lost over the past two days, topping early gainers at S$6.65, up 15 cents.
Creative Technology saw more profit taking, dropping S$1.70 to S$30.10 in the opening 90 minutes.
Foreign tranches of DBS and OCBC banks fell S$0.70 to S$19.00 and S$0.20 to S$14.60 respectively.
